title: Launcher Subsystem Dynamic Attributes
description: Dynamic attributes of the launcher subsystem, defining the muzzle locator, fire animation, and remaining ammo feedback outputs.

definition.description: Resource location of the subsystem model, pointing to the corresponding launcher subsystem static attribute definition file.

locator.description: Muzzle locator name. Projectiles are fired from the world transform of this locator.

fire_animation.description: Animation name played on fire, keyed in the part's animation set. Defaults to 'fire'. Same-name animations restart from 0; multiple launchers on the same part must use different names to avoid interrupting each other. A missing animation triggers a single warning and disables the fire animation.

ammo_outputs.description: Remaining ammo feedback output channels and targets. Optional.

ammo_discovery_targets.description: Feed source query table: service channel to target names. The launcher runs a read-only discovery over this table on structure changes: an autoloader found this way owns the loading, while an ammo rack becomes a delivery target only when the model declares a human stage (human_reload_time > 0) — that is the manual-from-rack path. When a channel reaches both, both enter the candidate set and the router picks the earlier one by estimated time to the next round.

loader_discovery_targets.description: Crew query table of the human stage: crew channel to target names. Only the manual-from-rack path uses it — an autoloader has its own table because the human stage belongs to the mechanism's flow. The usual form is {"crew_loader_reload": ["local"]} — local is every SubPart of the part, so a seat is found as soon as it declares the same channel in its own loader_discovery_inputs; two turrets built in two parts stay isolated by local. Only meaningful when the model configures human_reload_time. Channels are handshakes for discovery only and carry no loading commands.

loader_time_multipliers.description: Post time multipliers: crew channel to how convenient that post is for loading this weapon (dedicated loader 1.0, gunner 2.0); keys are the query table's channel names. It belongs to this discovery relation, not to the seat globally — the same person loading another weapon can have another multiplier. Undeclared channels are 1.0; zero, negative and non-finite values are decoding errors. Two seats with the same number load at the same speed. When several channels reach the same seat, the lowest multiplier among them applies: a seat yields one candidate and multipliers never add up.
